title: Manager activation kit — cross-functional first 30 days
body:
Purpose:
Provide a pragmatic, cross-functional 30-day activation kit for newly hired or promoted engineering managers (IC->Mgr) to accelerate impact, reduce context-switch friction, and standardize the manager onboarding experience across teams. This kit bridges people-ops, eng leadership, product, and SRE touchpoints.

Scope and assumptions:
- Intended for first-time managers and newly promoted managers inside engineering orgs.
- Complementary to team-specific onboarding plans from the hiring manager.
- This document is a living kit: check linked artifacts for role-specific addenda (e.g., dedicated, serving-runtime, SRE).

High-level objectives (first 30 days):
1) Establish relationships and regular cadences with direct reports and key partners (product, design, SRE, infra).
2) Deliver at least one incremental team improvement (e.g., retro, sprint tweak, triage policy) to demonstrate early impact.
3) Own simple operational duties (oncall handoff, staff hiring plan input) and understand team metrics.
4) Complete core compliance and HR steps.

Pre-start (before day 0):
- people-ops: provision laptop, access, ID, and manager-specific tooling (1password groups + manager playbooks).
- hiring manager: send welcome note with 1) first-week schedule, 2) org map, 3) prioritized 30/60/90 goals draft.
- assign onboarding buddy (peer manager or senior IC).

Week 1 — Orientation & listening:
- Day 1: org welcome, HR forms, security brief, infra access.
- Meet direct reports 1:1 (30–45m): focus on relationship, context, what to stop/start/keep.
- Meet product partner (30m) and tech lead (30m): alignment on roadmaps and dependencies.
- Run a short team intro (15m) to set manager expectations: communication norms, office hours, 1:1 cadence.
- Complete mandatory compliance trainings (security, privacy).

Week 2 — Context & diagnostic:
- Shadow two team ceremonies (standup, planning, retro) to observe rituals.
- Review team metrics dashboard: latency, error budgets, SLOs, deployment frequency, incident count.
- Read three priority docs (arch overview, oncall runbook, recent postmortems).
- Deliverable: one-slide "team health snapshot" for manager + hiring manager review.

Week 3 — Small experiments & operational ownership:
- Identify one low-risk process change (e.g., async PR template, daily triage window) and pilot it.
- Take ownership of oncall rotation updates and verify handoff checklist.
- Hold skip-level intro with up to two ICs (30m) to hear upward signals.
- Set hiring priorities with people-ops: must-have skills, leveling recommendation, interview panel suggestions.

Week 4 — Align & commit:
- Present 30-day retrospective: what was learned, decisions made, proposed 60-day plan.
- Establish recurring cadences: 1:1s with directs (weekly/biweekly), skip-levels, leadership syncs, team-all.
- Confirm performance expectations and calibration approach with manager peers.
- Ensure hiring reqs are submitted and interview rubric tailored for role.

Hiring and interview rubric guidance (quick reference):
- Structure: screen -> technical deep-dive -> systems design / leadership -> culture & role fit.
- Anchors per stage (use 1–5 scoring):
  - Screen: clarity of communication, baseline technical competence (3+ is acceptable).
  - Technical deep-dive: problem decomposition, tradeoffs, debugging approach.
  - Systems design: capacity/latency reasoning, operational considerations (SLOs, rollback plan).
  - Leadership / collaboration: examples of mentorship, conflict resolution, cross-team influence.
  - Culture fit: alignment to Redwood values (productivity, reliability, developer-first empathy).
- Evidence rubric snippets (to include on interview forms):
  - "Candidate explained tradeoffs and proposed rollback path" (yes/no + notes).
  - "Provided concrete examples of mentoring or hiring" (behavioral anchor).
  - "Demonstrated operational awareness: incident handling steps and blameless postmortem framing."

Early onboarding checklist (to close in first 30 days):
- [ ] HR payroll + benefits complete
- [ ] Manager badge and building access
- [ ] SSO + 1Password groups + repo access established
- [ ] Oncall routing verified and first oncall shift scheduled
- [ ] 1:1 cadence scheduled for next 90 days
- [ ] Hiring needs documented and requisition started if needed
- [ ] Team metrics dashboard shared and annotated
- [ ] Buddy check-ins scheduled (weekly x4)

Coaching & performance calibration notes for people-ops:
- Provide managers a short "how to run 1:1" cheat-sheet and a 45-minute coaching clinic in week 6.
- Encourage pre-calibration packet for new managers: sample calibrated feedback on 3 anonymized ICs.
- Use interview recordings (if consented) as coaching inputs for panel improvement.

Edge cases & escalation paths:
- If no hiring manager onboarding plan was provided, escalate to hiring manager + people-ops for joint plan within 72 hours.
- If oncall not staffed within two weeks, contact SRE lead to assign temporary coverage.

Notes to people-ops ops lead (practical tweaks observed in pilots):
- Provide a short "first-week sprint" template with blocked time for focus and meetings.
- Host a monthly manager sync for new managers (first 90 days cohort) to share tips and small wins.
- Track a lightweight "manager happiness" pulse at day 30 and day 90.

Appendix — quick links and templates:
- Manager 1:1 template: https://confluence.redwood/people/manager-1on1-template
- Team health snapshot slide template: https://confluence.redwood/templates/team-health
- Interview panel rubric: HR-INT-2024 (see linked artifacts)

Open questions / follow-ups for next revision:
- Add tailored variant for managers in Dedicated / Private product teams (hardware + customer SLAs).
- Consider an optional micro-course for first-time managers on incident leadership.
- Evaluate pairing new managers with cross-org mentors outside eng to broaden perspective.

Owner & maintainers: people-ops (Aisha Patel primary), engineering onboarding squad for technical addenda.

Last updated: 2025-05-03 (in_review)
